text:
Maya: quick handoff — I'm off in 10. TL;DR: incident resolved for main customer-facing embed route, still seeing elevated 503s for a small EU subset. Primary for next 6h: @Leo, Secondary: @Sam. Runbook links below.

Maya: What happened — around 03:12 UTC we saw a sudden rise in 503s from embeddings-usw -> eu-west routing path. Pager fired, autoscaler reacted and scaled up but new nodes hit prewarming GC and C10 queueing. Some nodes failed healthchecks and were cycled which made a small cohort (~2% traffic) see sustained 5xx for ~18m.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT created: INC-2026-1453 | embeddings-503-spike | Severity: P2 | Affected: embeddings-usw -> eu-west path | Pages: 2 | Assigned: Maya, Leo

oncall-bot: Pager escalations: 03:15 -> 03:20 -> oncall escalation to secondary

Leo: thanks. Current status as of last check (03:45): overall traffic normal, global 95p token latency back to baseline, 503 rate for primary pool <0.1%, EU subset still ~1.4% but trending down. I forced a graceful drain on the two unhealthy nodes and bumped the prewarm timeout to 45s for that pool.

Sam: noted. Who did the canary? I saw a deploy-bot message earlier.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy: model/embedding-v2 -> route embeddings-usw | started 03:10 | finished 03:14 | no regression flagged

Rui: FYI the canary was unrelated but coincided which made debugging noisy. Root cause looks like transient disk IO spike on the eu-west NAT gateway pair (cloud provider). We opened ticket with infra and added kdump traces.

Maya: Actions taken before I go:
- drained two failing nodes, replaced with fresh instances (autoscaler handled capacity)
- raised prewarm timeout from 20s -> 45s for eu-west pool
- temporary routing split: 5% eu-west traffic routed to fallback model variant (embedding-v1-quant) to reduce pressure
- alert thresholds adjusted: 5xx alert lowered to 0.5% for eu-west for next 2h so we detect recurrence quickly

Maya: Runbooks and links: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/embeddings-503-response (see sections "quick mitigations" and "fallback routing"), escalation playbook: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/oncall-escalation

Leo: immediate next-steps for you @Leo: watch eu-west 5xx and p95 latency for embeds; keep fallback split at 5% for 1h and then evaluate. If 5xx stays >0.5% for 10m, execute emergency full-fallback to embedding-v1-quant (runbook step 4).

Sam: secondary tasks: review recent infra changes (NAT, network policy) and confirm with infra team that IO spike was transient. If infra team can't confirm, we should keep fallback and prep for a cross-region shift.

Rui: I've filed INF-8812 with cloud provider, added traces, and requested a post-mortem link. Also collected kernel oops and instance boot logs (location: s3://redwood-ops/incident/INC-2026-1453/).

Maya: Customer impact: visible to a small subset (European customers routed through eu-west) — we flagged top 3 affected customer accounts to sales & CS at 03:28 and offered temporary mitigation. No broad customer outages.

Leo: Communications: I'll post a short note to #customer-impact and ping CS with the current status. If we need a longer incident report I'll draft in the morning.

Sam: quick checklist for next shift:
- Confirm eu-west 5xx <0.5% and remove fallback routing after 60m stable
- Validate autoscaler prewarm change hasn't regressed memory/p95 for cold-starts
- Re-run regression evals for embedding-v2 against small prompt set (links in runbook)
- If reoccurs, follow runbook: full fallback -> emergency rollback -> open full-SEV

oncall-bot: Note: follow-up reminder set for 1h to re-evaluate fallback routing and thresholds.

Maya: Closing notes: logging tags used in this incident: tag:inc-2026-1453, tag:eu-west-nat-io, tag:embed-fallback. If you need me after I'm out, pester on pager or DM but prefer email unless it's urgent. :wave: Good handoff.

Leo: ack. I'll be primary. Sam will cover secondary and take the bridge if pages escalate. Leaving a sticky for next steps in the runbook. :thumbsup:

Sam: acked. I'll follow up on infra ticket and update this thread when done.

Rui: I'll drop the trace summary here when provider responds.

Maya: thanks team — handing off now.
